cinematic.note: Generic daylight glasshouse. Nothing filmic reached the render: on a cast render composition is locked, so the directive has nothing left to say.

cozy.note: Bright daylight and a tighter waist-up crop. Sonnet wrote 'warm golden lamplight' but the render shows none of it.

epic.note: Wider full-body framing and cool mist. The only thing 'epic' did was shrink the figure, the failure mode the looks matrix flagged for composition words.

nostalgic.note: Warm amber light and fallen leaves on the path; reads as a fond autumn afternoon. One of three vibes that survived the v1 route.

peaceful.note: Bright daylight, grey sweater, half turned away; identity 0.48, the lowest of the round. Indistinguishable from cinematic and cozy.

dark.note: Foggy, desaturated and moody, and the velvet jacket finally rendered. But it is overcast day, not night; no candle, no deep shadow.

ethereal.note: Bright daylight with magenta bougainvillea. No glow, no haze, no pearl light.

arcane.note: Amber lanterns everywhere and glowing blossoms on the pond. Magic read clearly because the directive names concrete light objects.

enchanted.note: Plain daylight. 'Glittering motes' and 'colors glowing brighter than life' produced nothing.

nightshade.note: Teal mist and orange orchids, but it restyled the locked velvet jacket into a leather adventurer coat: the vibe leaked into the wardrobe.

golden_hour.note: Sunset amber pouring through the glass, teal sky, wet reflective floor, a lit gazebo. The best card of the round and proof a light-first vibe works.

blue_hour.note: Amber lanterns lit and a cooler cast, but the sky is still daytime. Sonnet wrote cobalt dusk; Flux kept the day.

moonlit.note: Sonnet wrote a full-moon night with silver light and indigo shadow; Flux rendered overcast daylight with petals on the pond. The clearest proof the scene text arrives too late.

stormlight.note: Slightly stormy grey light. No thunderheads, no sun shafts, no drama.

festive.note: No string lights, no confetti. Instead flying koi and a giant lantern: Flux turned 'drifting' into fish. The one render that went wrong rather than flat.

after_rain.note: Warm and faintly damp; misses the wet mirror surfaces and beaded drops that make the vibe.

sun_drenched.note: Bright saturated tropical light did arrive, but the face drifted (full beard, open shirt, identity 0.59).

spotlight.note: Even daylight everywhere. No spotlight, no dark surroundings, no beam.

aurora.note: Sonnet wrote the aurora sky; Flux rendered day with lanterns and painted the coat green instead (the palette leaked into the wardrobe).

prism.note: Plain daylight. No refractions, no rainbow arcs, no iridescence.
